info.title: Continuous LLM Evaluation & Regression Testing Platform API
info.summary: Release-gate system of record for AI quality.
info.description:
Specification only; no implementation exists. Serialized as JSON rather than YAML so the contract is validatable with the Python standard library, which keeps Phase 3 free of a dependency manifest.

Every operation and schema carries an `x-requirements` extension naming the requirements it realises. Traceability is therefore derived from this document mechanically rather than restated in a matrix that can drift.

tags.name: registry
tags.description: Versioned prompts, models and systems. A run identity is only meaningful if every element it names is immutable.

tags.name: experiments
tags.description: Reproducible experiment tracking, and reproduction of a past run from its captured identity.

post.description: Freezes run identity before execution begins, estimates cost, and reserves budget. Rejects rather than partially executes when the estimate exceeds budget.

409.description: Rejected before execution because the cost estimate exceeded the budget.

get.summary: Retrieve a run with its completeness and reproducibility state

post.description: Leaves a consistent and clearly incomplete record.

200.description: Cancellation accepted; the run settles to the cancelled terminal state.

409.description: The run already reached a terminal state.

get.description: A sample that failed, timed out, or abstained carries a resolution state and no numeric score.

post.summary: Evaluate a candidate against an approved baseline and return a gate decision
post.description: The CI entry point. Resolves the approved baseline without requiring the caller to restate it. Returns a decision whose outcome distinguishes platform failure from every quality outcome, and which always carries the evidence behind it.

200.description: A gate decision was reached. Note that a decision of `hard_fail`, `insufficient_evidence`, or `not_comparable` is a successful API call: the platform did its job. Only `503` indicates the platform itself failed.

get.summary: Retrieve a past gate decision and its evidence
get.description: Answers, for any past release decision, what evidence supported it, who approved it, and under which policy and statistical method version.

schema.description: The same decision as prose, carrying the same evidence: every criterion, the rule that fired, the interval and the sample size.

post.summary: Waive a gate decision under an audited policy exception
post.description: Requires an actor, a justification, and an expiry. An exception without all three is not representable.

get.summary: List dataset versions with approval and release state

post.description: Draft versions are mutable. Schema violations are rejected, never coerced. Quality checks run before the version can be approved.

422.description: One or more examples violated the declared schema and were rejected.

post.summary: Approve and release a dataset version
post.description: Releasing makes the version an immutable snapshot and baseline-eligible. Requires recorded human approval.
Pins dataset, prompt, model configuration, suite, evaluator and judge versions. A change to any pinned version makes a later comparison not comparable.
Destroys content-class artifacts and demotes referencing runs from reproducible to auditable. Decision records and audit records survive. The request itself is audited.

202.description: Erasure accepted. Affected runs are listed so the loss of replay fidelity is visible rather than silent.

409.description: An active baseline pins the target; an audited override is required.

get.description: Append-only. Not deletable by the actors it records.

post.summary: Add a version to a prompt
Publish a prompt version, making it immutable

200.description: The published version. Publishing an already-published version is not an error.

get.summary: Retrieve the captured identity of a run, component by component

post.summary: Assess whether a run can be reproduced from its captured identity, naming every element that cannot
Add a version of a gate policy, with its criteria
post.description: Criteria are part of the version rather than editable beneath it: freezing the version and leaving its criteria mutable would freeze the wrapper and not the contents.

post.summary: Publish a gate policy version, freezing it
post.description: A published version cannot be modified, and neither can its criteria. A version with no criteria cannot be published: a gate that governs nothing reports `pass` for every release, which is worse than no gate because it carries the appearance of one.

post.summary: Approve a baseline, superseding the one it replaces
post.description: One approved baseline exists per project and suite version, so REQ-F-09-7 can resolve 'the approved baseline' without the caller restating it. Approving supersedes the previous holder in the same transaction: between two transactions there would be a moment with none.

bearerAuth.description: Scoped credential. Every authorization decision is enforced server-side.

idempotencyKey.name: Idempotency-Key
idempotencyKey.description: Duplicate delivery must not double-count results or cost.

correlationId.name: X-Correlation-Id
correlationId.description: Correlates the request through workflow, model call, evaluator, judge, artifact and gate decision. Generated if absent.

Forbidden.description: Authenticated but not authorized. Cross-tenant attempts fail here and are audited.

NotFound.description: No such resource within the caller's tenant scope.

PlatformFailure.description: The platform failed. This is never a quality verdict, and callers must not interpret it as one.

Decimal.description: Exact decimal as a string. Money and token quantities are never floating point.

Problem.description: RFC 9457 problem details, extended with a category that separates platform failure from every other outcome.

detail.description: States which stage failed and what the caller can do about it.

category.description: `platform_failure` means the platform failed and no quality claim is made. A quality failure is never reported as a Problem; it is a successful gate decision.

Completeness.description: Five states, four of which are not success. Never a boolean.

Reproducibility.description: Stored state, not inferred at replay time. `auditable` means content required for replay has been erased.

RunIdentity.description: Frozen before execution begins and never updated. The component-by-component form is at `GET /runs/{runId}/identity`; this is the summary carried on the run itself.

promptVersionIds.description: One per candidate that names a prompt version. Empty when no candidate does.

modelConfigurationIds.description: One per candidate. A run compares two or more candidates, so a single identifier could only ever describe one of them.

candidates.description: Two or more candidates compare model or provider configurations in one run.

IntegrationTier.description: How much intermediate state the caller exposes. Determines which evaluators are available; unavailable evaluators are reported as unavailable, never approximated.

Budget.description: Cost is estimated before execution and enforced during it.

completeness.description: Null until `executionState` is `terminal`. A run still executing has not ended in any of the five ways, and reporting it as `partial` would mean the opposite of what it is.

sampleCounts.description: Count of samples by resolution. Present so a caller can see that an incomplete run is incomplete without paging every sample.

CostSummary.description: Written when the run reaches a terminal state so a per-run answer needs no recomputation over history.

SampleResolution.description: Only `scored` carries a numeric score. The others never do.

exampleContentDigest.description: Null when the content has been erased.

ConsensusResult.description: Always carries a disagreement measure. A verdict without one is not representable.

state.description: `escalated` is terminal, not a retry marker.

UncertaintyInterval.description: A verdict without uncertainty is not a verdict.

Classification.description: `insufficient_evidence` and `not_comparable` are first-class outcomes, never error states, and never presented as `no_change`.

notComparableReason.description: Names the pinned version that differs.

abstentionReason.description: Present exactly when the classification is `insufficient_evidence`. An abstention that does not say what was missing is indistinguishable from a verdict that was never computed.

GateOutcome.description: Platform failure is deliberately absent: it is never a gate outcome and is returned as a 503 Problem instead.

baselineId.description: Omit to use the project's approved baseline.

GateDecision.description: Carries the exact evidence, the policy version and the statistical method version, so it can be re-derived under the rules that applied at the time.

evaluatedOutcome.description: What the evidence produced. Immutable. `outcome` may differ from it only by `exception_applied`, and only while an exception is in force — an exception never edits a decision (ADR-016).

justification.description: At least 20 characters, enforced by the store as well as here. 'ok' is not a justification.

demotedRunIds.description: Runs moved from reproducible to auditable, so the loss of replay fidelity is visible.

ExecutionState.description: Where the run is in its lifecycle. Distinct from `completeness`, which says how a run ENDED and is therefore absent until it has.

VersionState.description: A draft is mutable. A published version cannot be modified or deleted in any column, and a version referenced by a completed run is frozen whatever its state (REQ-F-01-1).

body.description: The prompt text. Its digest is derived here and never supplied by the caller: a caller-supplied digest is an assertion, and the identity model needs a fact.

IdentityComponentKind.description: Every kind is captured under REQ-F-07-1. `environment` is captured and deliberately excluded from the identity digest (ADR-014): two runs of the same measurement on different hosts are the same measurement.

inDigest.description: Whether this component contributes to the identity digest.

RunIdentityDetail.description: The captured identity as its components, not only as a hash. A digest can show that two runs measured the same thing; it cannot say what they measured, and REQ-F-07-3 requires naming the elements that could not be reconstructed.

ReproductionOutcome.description: `partially_reproducible` is never reported as `reproducible`. A reproduction that silently substituted the current version of a missing element would produce a number that looks like a reproduction and is not one.

CriterionSource.description: Where the paired values come from. Separate from dimension because a quality and a cost criterion are both paired per example, and conflating the two would make cost a special case.

MetricDirection.description: Which way is good. ADR-007 speaks of an interval entirely below zero as a regression, which holds only where higher is better; latency and cost run the other way.

CriterionAction.description: `pass` is deliberately absent. A policy that could map an abstention to a pass would erase the REQ-F-08-4 distinction at the point where it costs something; a team that does not care about a metric removes the criterion instead (ADR-016).

ComparisonResultKind.description: REQ-F-08-6 in the report: a reader who groups by this cannot average a rubric score into an exact-match rate.

RuleFired.description: Which rule produced the criterion's verdict. A report that says 'failed' without saying which rule failed is not the evidence REQ-F-09-4 asks for.

metricKey.description: For an evaluator source, the evaluator slug.

precisionThreshold.description: Interval width above which the comparison abstains. ADR-007 refused to set it from simulated data; a criterion without one abstains rather than guessing.

metricKey.description: For an evaluator source, the evaluator slug.

precisionThreshold.description: Interval width above which the comparison abstains. ADR-007 refused to set it from simulated data; a criterion without one abstains rather than guessing.

GatePolicyVersionRequest.description: The statistical parameters ADR-007 deliberately left unset are supplied here, by a person, and versioned with the policy so a decision made under them can be re-derived exactly.

GateCriterionResult.description: The exact evidence behind one criterion of the decision.
